extra.message: POST /login.html concatenates the attacker-controlled username and password into cur.execute(). A username such as admin' -- bypasses the password comparison. UNION queries can also extract database contents through the returned username.

POST /server.html passes the server parameter directly into os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). Shell metacharacters allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands with the application's operating-system privileges. Command output is returned in the response.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: The /static/(.*) route appends the captured path to static/ and opens it without checking that the resolved path remains inside that directory. Encoded parent-directory segments allow unauthenticated reads of application source, test.db, and other files readable by the process.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: GET /read concatenates the file query parameter into io.open('read/' + file_name) without validating directory boundaries. For example, file=../test.db returns the credential database, and additional ../ segments allow reading other files accessible to the process.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: SearchHandler passes the untrusted q query parameter as query. The template emits it using {% raw query %}, allowing an attacker-controlled search URL to inject HTML and executable script into the application's origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: SearchHandler also passes q as link, which is inserted unescaped into the JavaScript string var x='{% raw link %}'. A value such as ';alert(1);// terminates the string and executes attacker-controlled JavaScript when a victim visits the search URL.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The upload response includes final_filename without HTML escaping. Its extension comes directly from the multipart filename; a filename such as image. preserves executable HTML in the extension. self.finish() returns it with Tornado's default HTML content type. See [Tornado response handling](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/branch4.5/_modules/tornado/web.html).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: ContentHandler serves file bytes directly as HTML. An attacker can upload an HTML document through /upload, obtain its generated filename, and use /read?file=../../../../../../tmp/<filename> to serve that document under the application origin. A victim following this URL executes the stored script. Uploads have no content validation, and this response has no attachment disposition. See [Tornado response handling](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/branch4.5/_modules/tornado/web.html).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The application omits xsrf_cookies and implements no Origin or CSRF-token validation. An attacker-controlled page can submit a cross-origin form to /server.html, triggering server-side commands through the victim's browser. This also exposes deployments reachable by the victim but inaccessible directly to the attacker. Tornado requires explicit activation of [XSRF protection](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/branch4.5/guide/security.html#cross-site-request-forgery-protection).

debug=True enables traceback responses on the externally bound application. Requesting a nonexistent file through /read triggers an uncaught exception that exposes filesystem paths, source lines, and implementation details. This behavior is documented in [Tornado debug mode](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/branch4.5/guide/running.html#debug-mode-and-automatic-reloading).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: UsersHandler.post prints the complete login request body, including username and password, to standard output before authentication. Anyone with access to captured application output can recover submitted credentials.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The Users table stores literal passwords without hashing or salting, and the login handler compares submitted passwords directly against this column. Read-only inspection confirmed that all eight records in the shipped test.db contain the plaintext seed passwords. Database disclosure immediately reveals usable credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The source embeds eight fixed account passwords, including admin/admin. Although create_db() is commented out in main(), the shipped test.db already contains the matching accounts and passwords, which the login handler accepts. Anyone with this source knows valid credentials.

The application creates an HTTPServer without TLS configuration and binds it to every interface on port 7777. The login form submits credentials to this same origin. When accessed directly as configured, usernames and passwords travel over unencrypted HTTP and can be intercepted by a network observer.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: ContentHandler calls read_file.read() without a size limit or regular-file check on an attacker-selected path. Traversing to /dev/zero causes an endless read and memory exhaustion; selecting a blocking special file can stall the event loop. StaticHandler has the same unbounded-read pattern at lines 46-47.

The synchronous request handler waits in process.read() for ping to finish, blocking the application's single event loop. No execution deadline exists. Repeated requests delay every other endpoint, and attacker-supplied ping options can extend the wait substantially even without shell metacharacters.

Every unauthenticated upload persists attacker-controlled bytes in a new /tmp file. The application enforces no cumulative storage quota and never removes completed uploads. Repeated uploads within any individual HTTP request limit can exhaust filesystem space or inodes, disrupting the application and other processes using /tmp.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The password input uses type="text", displaying the complete password while the user enters it. Nearby observers and screen recordings can capture the credential. This is [missing password field masking](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/549.html).
